claim: The data covers 80 pairs of jeans, 40 men's and 40 women's, from 20 brands once inconsistent brand spellings are merged.
Women's front pockets average 14.3 deep at their deepest point, against 23.1 for men's.
Men's front pockets range from 20.0 to 28.0 deep and women's from 11.5 to 21.5, so the ranges barely overlap.
Only one women's front pocket, Abercrombie's Simone High Rise Slim at 21.5, is at least as deep as the shallowest men's front pocket (20.0).
Women's front pockets are also narrower: 15.2 wide at the opening on average, against 16.4 for men's.
Back pockets are close in size: men's average 16.0 high and 13.7 wide, women's 15.1 high and 13.3 wide.
In 29 of the 40 women's jeans the front pocket is shallower than the back pocket; this happens in none of the 40 men's jeans.
In all 20 brands the men's jeans have deeper front pockets on average than the women's; the gap is smallest at Abercrombie (2.5) and largest at Levi's (13.4).
code: d.assign(b=d.brand.str.strip().replace({'7 for all Mankind': '7 for All Mankind'})).pivot_table(index='b', columns='menWomen', values='maxHeightFront', aggfunc='mean').pipe(lambda t: (t.men - t.women).round(2).sort_values())

claim: Cut makes little difference for women: average front pocket depth is 14.3 for skinny, 14.4 for straight and 14.2 for boot-cut jeans.
Paying more does not buy deeper front pockets: the correlation between price and front pocket depth is -0.15 for women's jeans and -0.26 for men's.
